userImpact: An employee opening /people sees the directory render and work normally. Two role-gated side-fetches 403 silently: the Resource Pool filter dropdown shows only 'All pools' (no pools load) and the 'N on bench' header chip is hidden. The only user-visible artifact is console noise — one 'Uncaught (in promise) ApiError: Insufficient role for this operation.' from the resource-pools fetch. The page is NOT blank or broken; no error boundary trips.
rootCause: EmployeeDirectoryPage fires two role-gated fetches without any FE hasAnyRole gate. (1) fetchResourcePools() at frontend/src/routes/people/EmployeeDirectoryPage.tsx:139-141 runs unconditionally on mount with NO .catch() — `void fetchResourcePools().then((r) => setResourcePools(r.items));` — so the thrown ApiError(403) becomes an unhandled promise rejection (console-only). Backend GET /resource-pools (src/modules/resource-pools/presentation/resource-pools.controller.ts:52-55) requires resource_manager/admin/director/hr_manager → 403 for employee. (2) fetchEnrichedBench() at EmployeeDirectoryPage.tsx:170-183 (dsRefresh-gated) hits GET /people/bench, gated by STAFFING_ROLES (src/modules/project-positions/presentation/project-positions.controller.ts:346-353; STAFFING_ROLES in src/shared/auth/role-presets.ts:48-54 excludes employee) → 403, but this call HAS a .catch (line 177) that sets benchCount=null, so it is fully caught and produces no console error and no UI break. The 'page blank/broken' premise of the finding is FALSE: the directory's own data source GET /org/people is gated ALL_AUTHENTICATED_ROLES (src/modules/organization/presentation/person-directory.controller.ts:111-112) → 200 for employee, and React error boundaries (frontend/src/components/common/ErrorBoundary.tsx — getDerivedStateFromError/componentDidCatch only) do NOT catch async useEffect promise rejections. No global window 'unhandledrejection' handler exists to escalate. 403 is not 401, so the http-client refresh path (frontend/src/lib/api/http-client.ts:80-118) is not triggered.
suggestedFix: Gate both side-fetches behind hasAnyRole in EmployeeDirectoryPage.tsx. For resource-pools (line 139-141): wrap in `if (hasAnyRole(principal?.roles, RESOURCE_POOL_READ_ROLES)) { ... }` and add a `.catch(() => setResourcePools([]))` to eliminate the unhandled rejection regardless. For the bench count (line 170-183): add a hasAnyRole(principal?.roles, STAFFING_ROLES) guard so an employee never fires GET /people/bench (it already has a .catch, so this is hygiene to stop the wasted 403 round-trip). Minimal change: add the role guards + the missing .catch on fetchResourcePools.
pageState: Fully functional / partially degraded silently. Directory list renders (GET /org/people = HTTP 200). Resource Pool filter is empty ('All pools' only) because GET /resource-pools = HTTP 403. Bench chip hidden because GET /people/bench = HTTP 403 (caught). One console error: 'Uncaught (in promise) ApiError: Insufficient role for this operation.' from the un-caught resource-pools fetch. Error boundary does NOT trip — page is not blank or broken.
evidence: Live repro as employee ethan.brooks@itco.local on deliverit-test-v2.agentic.uz: GET /api/resource-pools -> {"error":"Forbidden","message":"Insufficient role for this operation.","statusCode":403} HTTP 403; GET /api/people/bench -> same body HTTP 403; GET /api/org/people?page=1&pageSize=2 -> {"items":[...]} HTTP 200. Source: EmployeeDirectoryPage.tsx:139-141 (fetchResourcePools, NO .catch, ungated), :170-183 (fetchEnrichedBench, HAS .catch line 177). http-client.ts:120-135 throws ApiError(message, 403) using backend message 'Insufficient role for this operation.' ('wa:' in the finding is the minified ApiError class name in the prod bundle). resource-pools.controller.ts:52-55 RequireRoles('resource_manager','admin','director','hr_manager'). project-positions.controller.ts:346-353 @Get('bench') @RequireRoles(...STAFFING_ROLES). role-presets.ts:48-54 STAFFING_ROLES excludes employee. person-directory.controller.ts:111-112 @Get() @RequireRoles(...ALL_AUTHENTICATED_ROLES) (directory loads for employee). ErrorBoundary.tsx:16,20 only getDerivedStateFromError/componentDidCatch (no async-rejection capture). No window 'unhandledrejection' handler in frontend/src.
